scope: Proposition 2.5 (Closure of controlled families) of the manuscript “Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy” (preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/etr-counting-hierarchy.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 141 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 151fe6144a42154d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Controlled families are preserved by each of the following operations, applied a fixed number of times: (i) sums and products over short index sets, with uniform bounds on the summands or factors; (ii) powers with short nonnegative exponents computable in polynomial time, and substitution of controlled polynomials for indeterminates; (iii) extraction of indexed coefficients in any subset of the indeterminates, and differentiation in one variable to a short indexed nonnegative order. In the first operation the index domain is specified in polynomial time; more generally, an available predicate A(w, i) may restrict the indices when polynomial-time uniform bounds for the unrestricted domain are retained. This predicate depends only on the primary word and the family index, not on an evaluation prime or evaluation point. All resulting bounds and prime cutoffs are computable in polynomial bit time from the primary family data. In particular, they are independent of evaluation primes.
